summary.text: Woman in her 60s referred with an unruptured aneurysm (>5 mm, right ICA-PCom junction) found at another hospital; angiography confirmed it and preventive treatment was planned. She reported a metal-allergy history and patch tests were positive for nickel and gold.

Titanium clipping was considered but she preferred an endovascular approach; coil embolization using only nickel-free i-ED coils was planned. After DAPT started 10 days before, six i-ED coils were deployed under general anesthesia, ending with a small neck remnant and no branch occlusion on final angiography.

Next-day DWI MRI showed an asymptomatic punctate right basal ganglia lesion. DAPT was reduced to a single agent for 1 month; no allergic symptoms occurred over more than 1 year (18 months in Table 1) and corticosteroids were not given.

summary.text: Woman in her 70s with a saccular 11 mm left vertebral artery aneurysm found at a local clinic; she reported metal allergy and patch testing was positive for nickel.

Stent assistance was deemed essential, but Enterprise, LVIS, Neuroform, Pipeline Flex and FRED were excluded for nickel content; the Surpass Evolve (reported lower nickel) was chosen off-label with ethics approval and consent. After DAPT started 10 days before, a 4.0 × 20 mm Surpass Evolve was deployed across the neck under general anesthesia.

Final angiography showed contrast stagnation with persistent filling of the aneurysmal body. No apparent allergic symptoms occurred over more than 6 months (11 months in Table 1); single antiplatelet therapy was planned for 1 year after treatment and corticosteroids were not given.

summary.text: Woman in her 70s with a known right ICA C2 segment aneurysm (snowman-like, 5.1 mm) that gradually enlarged over several years; she reported metal allergy and a patch test at another hospital was positive for nickel.

Endovascular treatment was considered given rupture risk; coiling was judged unlikely to succeed, so the Surpass Evolve (reported relatively low nickel content) was chosen off-label with ethics approval and consent, with antiplatelet therapy the same as Case 2. Under general anesthesia a 4.0 × 15 mm Surpass Evolve was deployed from just proximal to the PCom to the C4 segment, fully covering the neck.
No allergic symptoms occurred over more than 6 months (9 months in Table 1) and corticosteroids were not given.

article_limitations: Only the three original present cases form the roster. Table 1 literature cases/cohorts (Tonetti, Wallace, Baranoski, Tsuji, Aamir et al.) and the review discussion are background, not accepted facts for any index patient; no linkage of a literature row to an index patient is stated.

The abstract mean follow-up of 12.7 months is an aggregate and is not assigned to individuals; individual Table 1 follow-up values (18, 11, 9 months) are retained, and the narrative gives only lower bounds (more than 1 year, more than 6 months).
No calendar dates are given; times are literal relative expressions only.
Antiplatelet agents and doses, and the exact aneurysm size in Case 1, are not reported.
